summary: Join our training on Precision Agriculture and Remote Sensing. Equip yourself with essential skills for climate resilience and sustainable farming practices.
lede: Precision agriculture and remote sensing combine satellite imagery, field observations, and weather data to support climate-resilient farm decisions. For agronomists, farm managers, GIS analysts, and resilience specialists, the training covers screening seasonal imagery, interpreting vegetation indices, and mapping crop stress and irrigation priorities. Learners also practise validating findings in the field and turning assessed risks into intervention zones and a resilience roadmap.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who use agricultural, geospatial, environmental, and climate data to guide production or resilience decisions. It suits intermediate to advanced learners with practical exposure to farm operations, GIS, agronomy, Earth observation, or climate adaptation.
audience: Irrigation Managers using soil-moisture evidence to schedule
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to agricultural operations, GIS, agronomy, Earth observation, environmental monitoring, or climate adaptation. Basic map reading, spreadsheet use, and familiarity with farm or landscape data will help. No programming experience is required for completion, although optional Google Earth Engine scripting demonstrations may include simple JavaScript examples. Advanced topics such as AI-assisted classification, SAR interpretation, and automated monitoring are taught at conceptual awareness or operational application level rather than production engineering depth. Bring a laptop with a modern web browser. QGIS can be installed before delivery if available, while Google Earth Engine access depends on account eligibility and course setup.
